about: How a day is named at the start of a scene (owner, Nov 8, 2:20 p.m.: 'If it's June 7th, it says first thing on June 7th. You head to the clerk's office and speak to Maria Patton.'): the part of the day and the date as people say it, 'first thing on June 7th'. Read by src/english/day-words.ts; the director passes the date and the minute of the day.

parts.said: In the middle of the night on {date}

landing.about: How the opening's landing names its day (Words lead, Nov 14, on #9242): after 'It's', the part of the day by the minute the player lands, and the date with no ordinal ('January 20'). Read by dayLanding in src/english/day-words.ts.

parts.said: the middle of the night on {date}

sinceOtherYear.about: A record's day in another year than the day a scene plays, told with its year (Fable A, Nov 13, rule 3: 'A date in another year is said with its year or as "last February". A bare month and day always means this year.'; Playtester P2, Hewitt NJ: 'stops you in the street about what happened on February 20th' on January 31st, a February a year gone). lastYear is the calendar year before the scene's; earlier is any year before that. Read by daySince in src/english/day-words.ts in place of the since row that names the date.

sinceAbout: A record's own day told as past from the day a scene plays (pool item words-day-end-scene-opens-next-midnight): 'yesterday', 'the other day', 'on January 3rd'; never a weekday, since a scene's opening names no weekday (owner, Oct 26: "it shouldn't say ... it's Tuesday in November"; src/director/scene.test.ts). Read by daySince in src/english/day-words.ts; the scene passes it to its lines as the fact since, which a sentence may use.

ahead.about: A later day as a friend says it when asking the player along (Words lead, Nov 15: the day is said as 'tonight', 'tomorrow night' or the day): the same day or the next, by whether the thing starts in the evening, else 'on' and the day from dayAhead. Read by dayAheadSaid in src/english/day-words.ts.
